cheng: Quick postmortem-ish notes from a 2h microprofile run on prod-staging. Dropped a Grafana dashboard + a pprof flame (link below). TL;DR: suspected kernel selector tiebreaker is picking a higher-SM kernel for short sequences which increases SM occupancy and hurts 99th tail on small-route workloads. Also saw KV cache hit-rate dip during burst windows, which amplifies token tail. dashboard: https://grafana.internal/r/rdw-runtime/prof-pprof-flame

maya: can you paste the flame snapshot? short thread please, we should keep this runnable before EOD :thumbsup:

cheng: pasted flame snippet + notable PromQL queries in the dashboard. flame shows hot path in kernel::dispatch -> select_kernel() with a lot of time spent in tiny kernels (kernel_small_seq) when batch sizes <= 4. Example flame excerpt:
```
# simplified stack (from pprof)
kernel::dispatch
  kernel_selector::select_kernel
    kernel_small_seq::run
    kernel_generic::run
```

ivan: interesting — sounds like selector heuristics are favoring better latency microkernels but costing SM utilization. do we have the selector decision trace?

cheng: yes, added selector.trace under the run artifacts. core condition that flipped was `sm_util_delta < 0.06` combined with `expected_tokens_per_batch < 12`. that made the tiebreaker prefer small_seq kernel which uses more SMs per warp. snippet from trace logic:
```
if sm_util_delta < 0.06 and expected_tokens_per_batch < 12:
  choose_kernel = small_seq
else:
  choose_kernel = generic
```

tunji: two quick asks: 1) can we add per-route token-level waterfall panels (decode vs kernel_exec vs memcpy vs kv_lookup)? 2) SM occupancy heatmap grouped by MIG slice + model route. those would show the coupling between kernel choice and slice saturation.

maya: +1 on waterfall. we need per-route KPIs too (p50/p95/p99 token-latency, kv-hit-rate, avg-batch-size). also add a panel for "kv-lookup latency distribution" — that spiked during the bursts in this run.

cheng: added a draft PromQL for token breakdown (feel free to copy):
```
sum by (route, phase) (rate(runtime_token_latency_seconds_bucket[1m]))
```
and an occupancy query to try: `avg_over_time(gpu_sm_utilization{gpu=~".*"}[5m])` joined with `gpu_mig_slice{slice!=""}` to produce heatmap. put both on the same dashboard row.

ivan: on KV: sounds like eviction behavior may be interacting with bursty traffic. observed pattern: kv-hit-rate drops ~6% when occupancy > 78% for >= 30s. can we add an alert that triggers when kv_hit_rate < 0.85 AND sm_occupancy > 0.78 for 1m? perf-bot: open a ticket? :robot_face:

perf-bot: Created perf ticket #PROF-4927 — "Investigate selector tiebreaker + KV hit-rate interaction" and attached trace + flame.

tunji: next steps I propose: 1) cheng — clone the runtime profiling dashboard into `runtime/experiments/tiebreaker-2026-03` and add the waterfall+sm heatmap panels (EOD). 2) ivan — PR with a conservative selector change: raise `sm_util_delta` threshold to 0.12 behind a rollout flag. 3) maya — add per-route KPI dashboards for the small-latency routes and schedule a 1h canary tomorrow morning.

cheng: I’ll do the dashboard clone now and attach the exact queries. pulling the pprof -> flame into the artifact store as `pprof-2065432100.tar.gz`.

maya: ok, thanks. if canary looks good we can unflag and push to prod. otherwise roll back and we have the perf ticket to reference. :white_check_mark:
